chunks: And Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

Ill omen for the traveler on his road is in six things: the crow cawing on his right, the dog spreading its tail, the howling wolf that howls in the man’s face while crouching on its tail, howling, then rising and then lowering itself three times, the deer crossing from right to left, the screeching owl, the gray-haired woman exposing her private part, and the mutilated she-donkey, meaning the one whose ear is cut off.

So whoever senses within himself anything from them, let him say: ‘I seek protection in You, O my Lord, from the evil of what I find within myself, so protect me from that.’ He said: ‘Then he will be protected from that.’

key_terms.اعْتَصَمْتُ بِكَ: I seek protection and refuge in You
key_terms.الذِّئْبِ الْعَاوِي: the howling wolf described as an ominous sight
key_terms.الشُّؤْمُ: ill omen or ominous sign for the traveler
key_terms.الظَّبْيِ السَّانِحِ: the deer crossing in a particular direction
key_terms.فَاعْصِمْنِي: so protect me and preserve me

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler say if he feels apprehension after seeing an ill omen on the road?
ai.summary: This hadith mentions certain signs regarded as ominous for a traveler and teaches a du'a to recite if one feels apprehension because of them. Its significance lies in directing the believer away from fear of created things and toward seeking protection from Allah through supplication.
